 JUDGMENT

The petitioners have filed this claim petition U/Sec 166 of M.V. Act, 1989, against respondents seeking compensation on account of death of one Sri.K.Shashi Kumar S/o K.Ramesh Babu, who died in Motor Vehicle Accident.
02.

The brief facts of the case of the petitioners is as under:
On 24.09.2023 at about 09.30 a.m, the said K.Shashi Kumar was proceeding/inmate in Car bearing No.KA-51-ML-5355 which was driven by its driver on NH-42 Road at Culvert No.140/2, via Kadari-Ananthapur Road, with high speed, in rash and negligent manner and dashed to the road side culvert No.140/2, as a result of which the said K.Shashi Kumar sustained head injury and succumbed to the injuries on the spot and petitioners have spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards treatment, transportation of deadbody and obsequies.

Prior to accident the deceased was hale and healthy and was aged about 29 years and was working as a Professor at Srinivas (SCCH-3) 4 M.V.C.No.528/2024 Ramanujan Institute of Technology (Autonomous) and also conducted tuition for degree students and also he joined Ph.D course and was earning Rs.50,000/- p.m.
After the accident the petitioners have lost their love and affection, unhappiness, financially loss and loss of dependency.
The deceased was the only earning member in his family and he look after the entire responsibility of his family members.

The accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of offending car and in this regard the Patnam Police have registered a case against Kuruba Bhargavi vs Umashankar Kolla on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3862384/
2 driver of offending car.

The respondent No.1 being the owner and respondent No.2 being the insurer of offending car, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.1,10,00,000/- with cost and interest at the rate of 12% p.a.
03.
On service of notice, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared before the tribunal through their counsels, but only the respondent No.2 has filed objections.

04. The respondent No.2 in its objections has denied the entire case of the petitioners and further denied the alleged accident, negligence of the driver of offending car and involvement of the offending car in the accident, age, avocation and income of deceased, (SCCH-3) 5 M.V.C.No.528/2024 nature of the injuries sustained by the deceased and expenses incurred by the petitioners and further denies existence of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident and its liability and contended that the driver of the offending car was not holding valid and effective driving licence and hence the owner has committed breach of terms and conditions of the policy and the compensation claimed is exorbitant and hence prays to dismiss the petition against respondent No.2 with costs.

05. On the basis of the above pleadings of the parties, the following Issues has been framed by my learned predecessor:-
ISSUES 01.
Whether petitioners proves that they are the LRs/dependents of deceased Sri.K.Shashikumar S/o K.Ramesh Babu?

02. Whether petitioners prove that deceased Sri.K.Shashikumar S/o K.Ramesh Babu was died on 24.09.2023 at about 9.30 a.m, in front of near M.Kottal, Mudigubba Mandal, Sri Sathya Sai District, Andhra Pradesh, due to rash and negligent driving of Car bearing registration No.KA-51-ML-5355 by its driver as alleged in the petition?
03. Whether respondent No.2 proves that driver of car not having valid license?
(SCCH-3) 6 M.V.C.No.528/2024 04.
Whether respondent No.2 proves that due to the negligence of the deceased.
Hence, respondent No.2 is not liable to pay compensation?
05. Whether petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount & whom?
06 . What order or award?

06. The petitioners in order to prove their case, petitioner No.1 is examined herself as PW.1 and got examined one witness as PW.2 and got marked 31 documents as Ex.P.1 to 31 and closed their side Kuruba Bhargavi vs Umashankar Kolla on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3862384/
3 evidence.
07.
By way of rebuttal, the counsel for respondent No.2 submits no oral evidence and respondent No.1 did not lead evidence, hence respondents evidence is taken as nil and closed their side evidence.
08. Heard both sides.
The counsel for the petitioners have filed written arguments.

09. My findings on the above Issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : In the Negative  Issue No.4 : In the Negative  (SCCH-3) 7 M.V.C.No.528/2024  Issue No.5 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.6 : As per final order  for the following:-
 REASONS 10. Issue No.1:- Petitioner No.1 in her affidavit stated that, she is the wife, petitioners No.2 to 4 are minor daughter and parents of the deceased.

To prove the said facts, she has produced notarized copies of Death certificate, Aadhaar card, Birth certificate, SSLC marks card, Intermediate certificate, Provisional certificate and Convocation certificate of deceased, Aadhaar cards of petitioners No.1, 3 and 4 and Birth certificate of petitioner No.2 and original Geneology tree as per Ex.P.11 to 17 and 21 to 25.
There is no dispute regarding dependency of the petitioners with the deceased.
These documents clearly goes to show that, the petitioners are the legal heirs and dependents on the deceased.
Hence, I answered Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
11. Issue No.2:- Petitioner No.1 got examined as PW.1 and she has given evidence in the form of the affidavit and she has reiterated the petition averments therein.

Though, she has been elaborately cross- examined by the respondent No.2 counsel, but nothing (SCCH-3) 8 M.V.C.No.528/2024 is brought on record to disbelieve the case of the petitioners that due to rash and negligent driving of the offending car by its driver, deceased sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident and died on the spot.
On perusal of exhibited documents, Ex.P.1 FIR registered at Patnam Police against driver of offending car.
Ex.P.2 is the Complaint shows that due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending car the accident took place, in which the deceased sustained injuries and later died.
Ex.P.3 is translated copy of Complaint.

M.Kottala Village, Mudigubba Mandal of Sri Sathya Sai District, which is not disputed.
Ex.P.6 is Accident inspection report shows involvement of offending car in the accident.
Ex.P.7 is Inquest report of deceased K.Shashi Kumar.
Ex.P.8 is translation copy of Inquest report.
Ex.P.9 is PM report of deceased K.Shashi Kumar shows death is due to shock and hemorrhage due to head injury.

Ex.P.10 is Charge sheet shows after investigation the Investigation Officer has filed Charge sheet against driver of the Car for the offences punishable U/Sec 338, 304(A) of IPC.
To disprove the case of the petitioners, the respondent No.2 did not lead evidence.
The oral and documentary evidence clearly goes to show that the accident has occurred due to the negligence on the part of the driver of offending car and deceased sustained injuries and later died.
Accordingly, Issue No.2 is answered partly in the affirmative.

12. Issue No.3 and 4:- In order to avoid repetition of facts and appreciation of evidence on record,
these two issues are taken together for common consideration and discussion.
13.
The respondent No.2 has taken specific contention that the driver of the car was not having valid licence and accident occurred due to the negligence of the deceased.

But in this regard the respondent No.2 did not examined any witnesses to prove its contention and in Charge sheet the Investigation Officer has not quoted any sections regarding negligence contributed by the deceased also and non-possessing of driving licence by the driver of the car.
Hence, the contention of respondent No.2 is untenable.
Accordingly, these Issues are answered in the negative.
14. Issue No.5:-
This issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the (SCCH-3) 10 M.V.C.No.528/2024 death of the deceased K.Shashi Kumar who died in the Motor Vehicle Accident.

The PW.1/petitioner No.1 in her evidence and pleadings has stated that prior to accident deceased petitioner was hale and healthy and was aged about 29 years and was working as a Professor at Srinivas Ramanujan Institute of Technology (Autonomous) and also conducted tuition for degree students and also he joined Ph.D course and was earning Rs.50,000/- p.m and petitioners have spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards treatment, transportation of deadbody and obsequies.
Due to untimely death of deceased, the petitioners are put to great hardship and lost love and affection and dependency, loss of mental agony etc.,.

15. In order to prove age of the deceased, the petitioners have produced Aadhaar card, Birth certificate, SSLC marks card of the deceased and according to which his date of birth is mentioned as 17.08.1994.
The alleged accident occurred on 24.09.2023 and hence it appears that as on the date of accident, the age of the deceased is 29 years.
Therefore, this tribunal has assessed the age of the deceased as 29 years as on the date of accident.

As per the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla (SCCH-3) 11 M.V.C.No.528/2024 Verma and Ors. V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and Ors. case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 26 to 30 is "17".
16.

On perusal of documents at Ex.P.18 to 20 and Ex.P.26 to 31, it discloses that the deceased was working in the said institution till March 2022 only and later he discontinued his job for further study to Ph.D and later he died on 24.09.2023 and at the time of accident he was not doing any job.

However, considering the documents, evidence of PW.2 and educational qualification certificates of the deceased, this tribunal assessed the reasonable monthly income of deceased is at Rs.25,000/-.
17.

In the case on hand, undoubtedly the petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioner No.2 is the minor daughter and petitioners No.3 and 4 are the parents of the deceased and they are dependents on the income (SCCH-3) 13 M.V.C.No.528/2024 of the deceased.

In view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co.
Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi & Others case, the future prospects or additional income should be added to monthly income of the deceased.

Since deceased was aged about 29 years at the time of accident and was self employee and he comes in the age group of below 40 years, 40% income should be added to the monthly income towards future prospects which would be result in the income to be (25,000 +
10,000) = Rs.35,000/-.

There are four dependents, it is appropriate to deduct 1/4th of the income of the deceased towards personal and living expenses of the deceased and then his monthly income would be (35,000 - 8,750) = Rs.26,250/-.
The income of the deceased for the purpose of determining the loss of dependency would thus be Rs.26,250/-.
As the deceased was aged about 29 years, the multiplier of 17 would have to be applied.
Consequently the claimants would be entitled for a sum of Rs.53,55,000/- (Rs.26,250/- x 12 x 17) towards loss of dependency.

18. In view of the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s. Pranay Sethi & (SCCH-3) 14 M.V.C.No.528/2024 Others case, in respect to loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses, the aforesaid amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every 3 years.

Ltd., V/s. Pranay Sethi & others case has calculated compensation as under:-

1. Loss of Dependency 53,55,000-00 (After deducting 1/4th of the income towards personal and living expenses)
2. Loss of spousal 48,400-00 consortium (For petitioner No.1)
3. Loss of parental 40,000-00 consortium (For petitioner No.2)
4. Loss of filial consortium 96,800-00 (For petitioners No.3 and 4)
5. Loss of estate 18,150-00 6.
Funeral expenses and 18,150-00 transportation of dead body Total Rs.55,76,500-00 20.

Accordingly I hold that, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.55,76,500/-
with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.

Regarding liability:- On service of notice, respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared and respondent No.2 has filed objections and contest the matter, but despite sufficient opportunity, they have not lead any evidence to disprove the case of the petitioners and to prove their contention including denial of issuance of policy.
Hence, it appears that on the date of accident policy was in force.
Hence, respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay above said compensation amount.
Respondent No.2 Insurance Company is directed to deposit above said compensation amount within two months from the date of filing of the petition till the date of deposit.
Accordingly, I answered Issue No.5 partly in affirmative.

Issue No.6:

In view of reasons assigned to Issue No.1 to 5, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners U/Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.55,76,500/- (Rupees Fifty five lakhs seventy six thousand and five hundred only) with interest at the (SCCH-3) 17 M.V.C.No.528/2024 rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this Judgment.
The petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioner No.2 is the minor daughter and petitioners No.3 and 4 are the parents of the deceased
were apportioned the compensation in the ratio of 70-10-10-10, in the award amount together with interest.

On deposit of the compensation amount together with interest, the petitioner No.1 is entitled to get release 70% of the award through E-payment directly to his account by obtaining the bank account details and remaining 30% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in her name.
The petitioner No.1 is at liberty to draw periodical interest.

Since the petitioner No.2 is minor, on deposit of the award amount with interest, her entire share amount shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any Schedule Bank till she attain age of majority in the name of her guardian with a liberty to draw accrued interest by her guardian on the said fixed deposit once in 3 months for the benefit of minor petitioner No.2.

On deposit of the compensation amount with interest, since the award amount of petitioners No.3 and 4 is meager one, entire award amount is ordered to be released in their favour through E-payment directly to their account by obtaining their bank account details.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi & Others case, the future prospects or additional income should be added to monthly income of the deceased.
There are four dependents, it is appropriate to deduct 1/4th of the income of the deceased towards personal and living expenses of the deceased and then his monthly income would be (35,000 - 8,750) = Rs.26,250/-.
The income of the deceased for the purpose of determining the loss of dependency would thus be Rs.26,250/-.
As the deceased was aged about 29 years, the multiplier of 17 would have to be applied.
18. In view of the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s. Pranay Sethi & (SCCH-3) 14 M.V.C.No.528/2024 Others case, in respect to loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses, the aforesaid amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every 3 years.
Accordingly, in the head of loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses, 10% is enhanced for period of every 3 years.
19. The claimant No.1 is the wife, claimant No.2 is the minor daughter and claimants No.3 and 4 are parents of the deceased.
Court in a decision reported in Magma General Insurance Company Ltd., V/s Nanu Ram alias Churu Ram reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130, the petitioner No.2 is entitled for Rs.40,000/- towards loss of parental consortium and petitioners are entitled for Rs.18,150/- each towards loss of estate and funeral expenses and transportation of dead body.

Accordingly I hold that, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.55,76,500/-
